nodes.label: A command group invoked without a subcommand exits 0 and prints help, so exit code alone cannot signal success
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-cf-cli-cloudflare-di-pc [ses_f16bcf263ffeP4ydwEeLdjZycU].md:L6813] "1. Group without subcommand (`cf zones`) → exit 0 + help" and "cf init" without a directory argument printed an Error box at exit 0 [same file:L4490]. The failure is silent in a script: the agent's own test battery recorded cf zones as PASS because it keyed on $?, when the command had made zero API requests. The same trap recurred once more when every candidate name was probed with --help, which prints help and exits 0 whether or not the leaf exists; the fix was a detector validated by a known-good and a known-bad command.
nodes.norm_label: a command group invoked without a subcommand exits 0 and prints help so exit code alone cannot signal success

nodes.label: Writing only the appended block to a temp file and then mv-ing it over the target destroys the original
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-cf-cli-cloudflare-di-pc [ses_f16bcf263ffeP4ydwEeLdjZycU].md:L8257] "I intended to do `.bashrc content + block` but I only wrote the block. I forgot to include the original content." The shape is `{ ...block... } > "$RC.tmp" ; mv "$RC.tmp" "$RC"`, which is a correct append idiom only when the redirect receives the original file's bytes. 72 lines of the user's .bashrc were replaced by the 123-line completion block; the symptom surfaced later as cf reporting "Not logged in". Recovered because the backup had been taken first, and the reported bug: "mv \"$RC.tmp\" \"$RC\" menimpa `.bashrc` dengan isi tmp yang hanya berisi blok, bukan isi asli + blok."
nodes.norm_label: writing only the appended block to a temp file and then mv ing it over the target destroys the original

nodes.label: Sourcing an env file below the interactive guard in .bashrc limits it to interactive shells only
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-cf-cli-cloudflare-di-pc [ses_f16bcf263ffeP4ydwEeLdjZycU].md:L8548] "`bash -lc` → guard at line 23 returns before line 66 (.env) → no token" and "`bash -c` -> never reads .bashrc -> no token" [same file:L8549]. The consequence is asymmetric between a human and an agent: the user always has a token in their terminal, while an agent shelling out does not, and the session only worked because the opencode process had inherited the environment from the launching terminal. Moving the sourcing above the guard fixed bash -lc but not bash -c, which reads .bashrc never and honours only BASH_ENV.
nodes.norm_label: sourcing an env file below the interactive guard in bashrc limits it to interactive shells only

Seven files that stand alone received the full block; eight CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md and .cursorrules files that already delegate to AGENTS.md received a three-line pointer. Two further structural facts changed the count from 17 paths to 15 written files: two .makemd/*.mdc matches were binary ZIP archives holding an LMDB database, and dawnbook/AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are symlinks to dawnbook/GEMINI.md.

nodes.label: A blocked postinstall script is harmless when the platform package already supplies the binary
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-cf-cli-cloudflare-di-pc [ses_f16bcf263ffeP4ydwEeLdjZycU].md:L1091] "So actually the blocked script was harmless here — the optionalDependency path already worked." npm 12 refused to run workerd's postinstall, which raised the prospect that local dev was broken. The shim at bin/workerd was 5.6K, which read like a missing native binary, until running it printed workerd 2026-09-26 matching workerd@1.20260926.1: the platform package @cloudflare/workerd-linux-64 is installed as an optionalDependency and the postinstall only downloads a fallback when it is absent.
nodes.norm_label: a blocked postinstall script is harmless when the platform package already supplies the binary

nodes.label: A missing tool in the verification harness reports as a defect in the thing under test
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-cf-cli-cloudflare-di-pc [ses_f16bcf263ffeP4ydwEeLdjZycU].md:L3844] "`jq: command not found`! So jq isn't installed. My \"gagal parse\" results for `cf cli search` and \"jq valid: TIDAK\" were because jq doesn't exist — not because JSON is invalid." Of five reported failures, one was a missing jq, one was head -c truncating JSON before validation [same file:L3705], three were guessed command names, and a sixth was cf zones passing on exit code alone. Installing jq and re-running turned the headline claim - JSON is the default interface - from an assertion into a verified fact.
